hyomen.name: Bio-Engineered Hyomen
hyomen.note: Lab-designed Hyomen iteration optimized for endurance and adaptive anatomy. Bipedal/Quadrupedal · Small–Moderate. Born at biological age 23; semi-hive consciousness; cannot be force-bred — each is individually engineered.

abilities.name: Enhanced Strength
abilities.effect: Passive (Self) · Automatic. Add half your current Neuronal Capacity Modifier to all Strength-based rolls.

abilities.name: Enhanced Anatomy
abilities.effect: Self · Instant · Automatic · Limit: forced success 1/scene. Gain Advantage on all Adaptation Rolls. Once per scene you may force one to succeed, but your following roll is halved after rolling.

hyomen.name: Spatians
hyomen.note: Void-born Hyomen evolved for life in the vacuum of space. Bipedal/Quadrupedal/Octopodal (4–8 limbs) · Moderate–Large. Breathe in open vacuum; enlarged skin pores act as biological propulsion in zero-gravity; each limb beyond 4 grants +1 Bonus Action per turn. The only known species to consistently evade the Nigraldi.

abilities.name: Space Modulation
abilities.effect: Self (Reaction) · Duration: 1 roll · Automatic · Limit: twice per encounter per limb beyond 4. On an AP Check failure, shrink to Small size classification and gain Advantage on your next Dexterity-based roll.

abilities.name: Evolved Body
abilities.effect: Self (Reaction) · Instant · Automatic. Convert incoming non-critical damage to a damage type of your choice before resistances apply. Cap: Supernatural-family damage cannot be converted.

hyomen.name: Neo-Humans
hyomen.note: Retain 80% of the original human genome — the most politically powerful Hyomen variant. Bipedal · Moderate. Cannot be subjugated: no Nigraldi override vector exists in their genome.

abilities.name: Awakened Visualization
abilities.effect: Passive, with Active triggers (Standard, Bonus, or Reaction) · Target: Field within 45 ft · Vector: Gaze/Ambient · Duration: Sustained · Resolution: related checks at Advantage, scaling with proximity. Passively sense and see magnetic and electromagnetic fields using your Perception Range Modifier; manipulate any magnetic field within a 45-foot radius. Transfer: apply a magnetic field to a target or surface that does not naturally possess one. Inverse: reverse the polarities and vector directions of an active field; magnitude governed by your Neuronal Capacity Modifier. Reshape: redefine a field's scale and geometry by inputting a designated Imaginary Number (IN) value — the field begins as a 1×1×1 cell; expanding it by 1 cell in any direction costs 5 ÷ Rank Multiplier.

abilities.name: Genetic Control
abilities.effect: Passive, with Active trigger (Standard, Bonus, or Reaction) · Target: Self · Duration: 1 Hour · Resolution: Curator review. Undergo a rapid physiological shift to activate latent, temporary genetic mutations within your own biology. Mutation Capacity: sustain up to (Recovery Rate Modifier × Rank Multiplier, rounded down) mutations simultaneously. Specific mutations and their physical capabilities are determined by Curator discretion.

hyomen.name: Ygloracellia
hyomen.note: The Hollow Will: individuals without purpose or reason, regarded as abominations glorified through an intrusive beauty that conceals their true forms. A Ygloracellia is a bipedal, Moderate–Large hybrid assembled from any number of species: mismatched arms, misplaced eyes, and other impossible anatomy. Regardless of the observer's origin, other species perceive an idealized, beautiful version of themselves. They proclaim Orialian descent and may bear animal traits or appear purely Hyomen, but all share ornate forehead horns that curve upward, often reaching 18 inches. Towering and physically imposing, they adorn themselves with makeup, jewelry, and piercings to proclaim their heritage like royalty. Their horns are the source of genuine magic and replace the body's Augo glands.

abilities.name: Uncertainty (Melam Hindrance)
abilities.effect: Side effect · Trigger: whenever an Innate occurs. Lose 5% of your total HP for each turn the Innate is maintained; if its duration is forcefully extended, lose 10% per turn instead. Once these losses reach 35% of your total HP, permanently lose 20% of your total HP and become incapable of recovering it. After that permanent loss occurs, gain a Torment: a physical or mental ailment with bonuses and drawbacks, determined through Curator's Desecration.

abilities.name: Light Eater
abilities.effect: Self (Reaction) · Duration: 1 roll · Automatic · Limit: none. Take the properties of Trans-Modification and Materialization, using Trans-Modification to invert Materialization's effects. This applies particularly to phenomena with Emission among their properties: take that property and modify it to increase Light Eater's Virulence.

abilities.name: Overzealous
abilities.effect: Self (Bonus) · Duration: 2 minutes · Resolution: after the duration. Using your Melam forces Divination around you, allowing you, once, to see an action one second before it happens. Each turn, lose one Advantage from Dexterity, Evasion, or movement rolls. Modifiers to those rolls are hard-capped at +4; when a roll uses a derived-statistic modifier, it is capped at +10 instead.

voaulton.name: Droid
voaulton.note: Fully synthetic descendants of the Voaulton — all organic parasitic instincts removed. Bipedal/Quadrupedal/Hybrid · Moderate–Large. Builders of the Mundus Machines; actively feared by the Nigraldi.

abilities.name: Modulation
abilities.effect: Self (Active) · Duration: Sustained · Automatic. Instantaneously restructure your physical form within control parameters and current security clearance tier. Each restructure is a Bonus Action; clearance disputes go to the Curator.

abilities.name: EMP
abilities.effect: Target: Area · Vector: Burst · Instant · Area: Radius 40 ft · Resolution: Endurance save (machines/electronics) · Limit: 1 free use per encounter. Redirect incoming damage outward as an electromagnetic pulse: unshielded machines and Grade 1–2 electronics in radius (attacker included) fail until the end of next round. Additional uses cost Synaptic Space or sacrifice modular limbs.

voaulton.name: Cyborg
voaulton.note: The 'Father Species' — organic-machine hybrid; parasitic ancestry sublimated into a healing and teaching role. Bipedal · Small–Moderate. Key figures in Northern Territories infrastructure; politically vulnerable for their Tauron lineage.

abilities.name: Hacking
abilities.effect: Target: 1 Creature · Vector: Reaction to being struck · Instant · Resolution: Automatic on qualifying trigger · Limit: once per round per individual creature. When struck by a physical attack, force the attacker's next action to automatically backfire. The malfunction stays within that action's own scope, Curator-narrated.

abilities.name: Circuit Transfiguration
abilities.effect: Target: 1 connected system · Vector: Contact · Instant · Resolution: contested by secured systems (operator's Control) · Limit: one command per merge. Merge with any connected technology and issue one command to the merged system: Halt, Detonate (its own listed yield, never more than 3d10), or Redirect.

voaulton.name: N-T1 (Novus-Tauron)
voaulton.note: Accursed remnants of the original Tauron species, despised universally. Bipedal/Quadrupedal · Moderate (arms and legs can extend to double length). External nervous system visible as crimson streaks; bio-node cluster at the neck. Covertly allied with the Xeno through the Deviants faction.

abilities.name: Forced Control
abilities.effect: Target: 1 Creature · Vector: Contact · Duration: 1 round · Resolution: forced AP Roll, then Strength Save or Adaptation Check · Limit: once per round; a target that resists is immune for the scene. On physical contact, initiate a forced AP Roll (even if one already occurred). On success choose: Nerve Grapple — restraint; the target makes a Strength Save to break free (Anchored (Soft) until it does) — or Neural Override — behavioral control; the target makes an Adaptation Check to resist commands, gaining the Subjugated condition on failure (capped control per the Hyomen conditions), scope per Curator discretion.

abilities.name: Elongation
abilities.effect: Self (Active) · Instant · Automatic · Limit: twice per 2-turn cycle. Extend any limb up to double its base length, reaching up to 40 feet. Each 10 feet extended beyond base reach costs −1 AP on the associated roll.

voaulton.name: Re-Varant
voaulton.note: Beings who find themselves unseen and undignified who wish to return to the glory of which they come from. Bipedal · Tiny. They exist as the stable yet Decomposed core piece of the tauron being the brain it developed and grew legs and arms, and it can burrow itself within Creatures that are Incapacitated and or already dead. Resurrection: as they take over bodies, if the host body is destroyed, the re varant can still live on to later take over another body main body can be extended beyond the host body to create extra limbs, extend base limbs, or reinforce base limbs bodies usually last roughly 25 years depending on how much the re varant repairs and cares for it.

abilities.name: Resurrection
abilities.effect: Target: 1 Creature · Vector: Contact · Duration: Indefinitely · Resolution: forced Density Check; a living host that can resist uses either a Power Check to physically repel the Re-Varant or a Recovery Save governed by Adaptation to resist biological takeover. As they take over bodies, if the host body is destroyed, the re varant can still live on to later take over another body main body can be extended beyond the host body to create extra limbs, extend base limbs, or reinforce base limbs bodies usually last roughly 25 years depending on how much the re varant repairs and cares for it.

abilities.name: Phylaction
abilities.effect: Target: 1 Creature · Vector: Contact · Duration: until Ceased Willingly · Resolution: forced Density Check, then Recovery Save governed by Adaptation · Limit: once per round; a target that resists is immune for the scene. Upon contact with the re varants main body (extensions, extra limbs, reinforced limbs, parts of the main body used as projectiles) afflict the opponents augo gland with Hollow Body Syndrome, all offensive abilities have damage reduced by the Re-Varant's Capacity Check and when non-offensive abilities are cast, the afflicted user must make a Recovery Save vs the Re-Varant's Capacity Check to successfully cast; lasts for 2 turns.

abilities.name: En-cTusion
abilities.effect: Type: Self (Active) · Duration: Instant · Resolution: Automatic · Limit: twice per 2-turn cycle. Trans-Modification or Emission abilities can be enhanced to increase damage by a Capacity Check or increase effectiveness (for example, movement abilities carrying the user farther) by a Capacity Check at the cost of 15 DHP.

mirga.name: Chimera
mirga.note: Forced evolutionary iteration of the Mirga — modular, segmented, massively adaptable. Bipedal through Amoeboid · Moderate to Colossal by configuration. 15 modular body segments: 2 face, 1 neck, 2 torso, 4 legs, 6 arms — each independent.

abilities.name: Multicellular Sentience
abilities.effect: Self (Active) · Duration: 2 full turns · Automatic. Detach any or all body segments intentionally; each detached piece gains its own Standard Action while the main body retains 1 Bonus Action. Detached pieces disintegrate and fully reform after 2 full turns. Cap: while 3+ segments are detached, your Dodge is at Disadvantage — a scattered body defends poorly.

abilities.name: Modularity
abilities.effect: Self (Active) · Duration: Sustained · Automatic · Limit: 8 times per hour. Transform any segment into any observed object — organic or inorganic. Never a specific creature's likeness (that is Perfect Mimicry's lane).

mirga.name: Pariacite
mirga.note: Your body is one of millions, each acting on its own — and in some cases biologically owning the others. Bipedal through Amoeboid · Moderate to Colossal. 2 modular body segments: each half of the body is independent and parasitic — built on Supercells.

abilities.name: Hostile Subsumption
abilities.effect: Target: 1 biological life form · Vector: Contact · Duration: Sustained · Resolution: Adaption Check, DC 25. On contact, force the check: on a failure you may meld with them — attached and riding their frame; both of you count as Anchored (Soft) until they win the re-check at the end of each of their turns. On a Critical Failure you take a piece of them, gaining their form as a transformation usable 5 times per encounter. Cap: melding never grants control of the host — Subjugated caps apply.

abilities.name: Modular Transformation
abilities.effect: Self (Active) · Duration: Sustained · Automatic. Transform either body segment into any observed object.

mirga.name: Matarilia
mirga.note: The variant most exploited for its ability to create new materials. Bipedal · Moderate. 15 modular body segments. Created to protect the Mirga — mass-producing elements for spatial shielding and experimental use.

abilities.name: Multi Material
abilities.effect: Self (Active) · Duration: Sustained (external limit: 3 minutes of Active time) · Automatic. Transform any of your segments into a chosen material; materials may be combined within your body to form new composite materials. No created material can exist outside your body for more than 3 minutes of Active time.

abilities.name: Material Create
abilities.effect: Target: Objects · Vector: Contact · Duration: Until-Broken (3-minute external limit) · Automatic. Transform any segment into an object of your material, or create an object of a composite material — the composite must contain the original material. External persistence obeys the 3-minute Active-time limit.

mirga.name: Scnial
mirga.note: Genetic stealers pioneered by the Nigraldi for infiltration — able to steal Incepts, but only dormant ones. Bipedal through Amoeboid · Moderate to Colossal. Organs can exist outside the body, generate encapsulated spaces, and pilot the main body remotely. Never to be trusted.

abilities.name: Genetic Stealer
abilities.effect: Target: 1 biological/animate being · Vector: Contact (grab) · Instant · Resolution: d20 sift, then Adaption vs target's Neuronal Capacity + Adaption Modifier · Limit: one stolen Incept held at a time. Grab on and roll a d20 to sift through their Incepts — the more dormant the Incept, the harder it is to steal. Win the follow-up contest and the dormant Incept is yours until it has been used a maximum of 6 times, after which it returns to its owner's pool. Only dormant/unmanifested Incepts — never an active, manifested one.

abilities.name: Permeation
abilities.effect: Target: 1 willing creature · Vector: Contact · Duration: up to 1 encounter · Resolution: Automatic (willing). A willing creature can give you access to their Genome; implant yourself inside it, and if you stay the maximum duration of an entire encounter, you can create a new form from their body and inhabit it, gaining half of their Incepts while wearing that form. Combining that form with your main form refreshes the usage count of any Incept stolen from them with Genetic Stealer back to 6.

oriyu.name: Radiant
oriyu.note: Oriyu whose energy field reached critical luminescence — living energy conduits past the threshold between organism and construct. Bipedal (energy corona) · Moderate. Condensed Energy Cores; constantly emit light, visible even in full darkness.

abilities.name: Radiant Cascade
abilities.effect: Target: Multi · Vector: Burst · Instant · Area: Radius 30 ft · Resolution: END Check or Disadvantage on next roll · Limit: twice per encounter. As a Standard Action, emit a blinding burst of energy: all targets in range make an END Check or suffer Disadvantage on their next roll.

abilities.name: Overload Absorption
abilities.effect: Self (Reaction) · Instant · Automatic · Limit: one absorption per round; max 3 Charges held; unspent Charges fade at scene's end. Absorb any energy-based attack: take no damage, storing 50% of its damage as an Overload Charge. As a Bonus Action, release a Charge at one target within 60 ft — dealing the other 50%.

oriyu.name: Nullified Oriyu
oriyu.note: Oriyu whose energy affinity inverted — zones of energy absence. Bipedal (translucent skin, dark vein-lines) · Moderate. Do not age; do not die naturally. Nomads with no terrestrial attachments; frequently misclassified as Null Genus users.

abilities.name: Energy Absence Aura
abilities.effect: Passive · Target/Area: nearby · Vector: Ambient · Always · Automatic. Passively suppresses nearby Genus energies at a low ambient level. In hybrid offspring, this may manifest as reduced Genus energy output or unusual resistance to energy-based effects.

abilities.name: Null Field
abilities.effect: Target: Area · Vector: Ambient · Duration: until end of scene — or until the Nullified Oriyu takes damage · Area: Radius 20 ft · Limit: one Field at a time. As a Standard Action, create a zone of energy suppression: all Genus-based abilities within the zone cost double Synaptic Space or AP to activate.

oriyu.name: Qerran
oriyu.note: Qerran are an accidental byproduct of Assembly processes that repeatedly transformed energy into flesh and flesh back into energy. Externally, they appear almost entirely Human. Their only consistent abnormalities are one or two iridescent eyes and an iridescent patch along the back of the neck that resembles a scale, scar, or thin shell. Little is known about their earliest formation beyond the fact that they were originally discarded as waste products of Assembly conversion procedures. Bipedal; externally Human-presenting · Tiny–Moderate. Bulbus Scalbs: the Qerran Nexus is distributed through dense iridescent energy organs called Bulbus Scalbs. Instead of generating the Augo Gland's internal bacteria solely within the gland itself, a Qerran generates and stores much of that activity throughout these Scalbs. Scalbs may appear as connected Patterns or irregular Splotches across the body. A Qerran naturally generates 2 new Scalbs per day; each individual Scalb withers at the end of its third day if it has not already been expended or destroyed. Qerran exist in an uncertain space between organism and conversion residue. Their outward Humanity conceals a distributed Nexus architecture capable of turning the body itself into a network of temporary energetic organs. Because detached Scalbs remain functional parts of that network, a Qerran can gradually spread the origin points of their own biology across other creatures.

abilities.name: Riven
abilities.effect: Type: Bonus Action · Target: Self / 1 chosen Pattern or Splotch · Duration: Immediate · Resolution: uses the copied ability's natural Check, Save, Roll Path, damage, and limits · Limit: each Bulbus Scalb may support Riven only once before withering. As a Bonus Action, focus on one Bulbus Scalb Pattern or Splotch and route an ability you are activating through it. The chosen ability must normally originate from you and must normally be able to activate within your Reach. Splotch — Overexpression: ability activates once per Scalb at half Reach; choose to double damage or add +1d10 to a Check/Save. Pattern — Sequence: ability activates once per Scalb in order, possibly targeting different valid creatures within normal Reach. A Scalb used for Riven becomes Spent and cannot be reused until withered, destroyed, or detonated.

abilities.name: Interitus
abilities.effect: Type: Standard Action · Target/Area: Self / chosen Bulbus Scalbs; fixed 40-ft burst · Vector: Biological Burst · Duration: Attached Scalbs persist until removed, withered, or detonated · Resolution: Physical Save — Recovery for unwilling creatures · Limit: each Scalb may undergo two detonations before dissipating. Rupture one or more Bulbus Scalbs, destroying the supporting flesh and initiating rapid regeneration. First Detonation — Scalb Dissemination: fragments affect all creatures within 40 ft; unwilling creatures make a Physical Save — Recovery, willing ones may accept attachment. Attached Scalbs remain part of the Qerran's Nexus and can still be targeted by relevant abilities. Second Detonation — Dissipation: previously detonated Scalbs fully dissipate, restoring 1d50 Synaptic Space to the current host or the Qerran if unattached.

oriyu.name: Asracion
oriyu.note: Across every universe exists some expression of the Mountains of Vesarin. Oriyu who devote themselves to what they call the Calling travel into these mountains and meditate until their bodies become mummified. To the Asracion this is not death, but the act of answering the Call — returning themselves to a Super Consciousness they believe exists beyond individual thought and identity. Those who emerge or remain functional after this transformation become Asracion. Bipedal; often desiccated or mummified in appearance · Tiny–Moderate. The Oriyu Nexus has integrated directly into the Asracion nervous system. This grants extreme sensitivity to the generation, movement, and release of energy through another creature's body. Within their effective sensing range, Asracion may perceive the energetic outline of a nervous system and the early formation of Augo Gland activity before an ability is fully executed. Asracion doctrine treats the nervous system as an incomplete boundary between individual consciousness and the greater Calling. Their abilities do not simply attack flesh — they interfere with the energetic sequence by which intent becomes biological action, allowing them to disrupt nearby Augo Gland execution or pull distant nervous energy out of alignment with the body that generated it.

abilities.name: Rescoene
abilities.effect: Type: Standard Action / Sustained · Target: 1 creature · Range: within half of your Reach · Duration: until the target succeeds its Save · Resolution: Mental Check — Perception vs Physical Save — Recovery · Limit: one creature affected by Rescoene at a time. Within half of your Reach, the Asracion sees the energetic outline of a creature's nervous system and the earliest stages of any action involving its Augo Gland — from bacterial generation and internal energy routing to the moment of execution. Choose one creature in range and make a Mental Check — Perception. The target opposes this with a Physical Save — Recovery. On a failed Save, the target gains Hollow Body Syndrome and suffers Double Disadvantage on any Check or Save directly required to activate, shape, sustain, control, or otherwise operate an Augo Gland ability. At the beginning of each of the affected creature's turns, it repeats the Recovery Save against the original Perception result. On success, Hollow Body Syndrome ends immediately. On failure, it persists until the beginning of that creature's next turn, when the Save is attempted again.

abilities.name: Serun
abilities.effect: Type: Bonus Action · Target: 1 creature · Range: beyond half of your Reach, up to your full Reach · Duration: until the target succeeds its Save · Resolution: Physical Save — Recovery · Limit: one creature Soft Anchored by Serun at a time. The Asracion reaches into the energetic structure supporting a distant creature's nervous system and pulls that energy forward, forcing the body's physical motion to lag behind its own neural transmission. A creature beyond half of the Asracion's Reach, but still within their full Reach, makes a Physical Save — Recovery. On failure, the creature becomes Soft Anchored. At the beginning of each of the affected creature's subsequent turns, it repeats the Recovery Save. On success, Soft Anchor ends immediately. On failure, it remains Soft Anchored until the beginning of its next turn, when the Save is attempted again. Serun does not affect creatures within half of the Asracion's Reach; its energetic pull requires separation between the Asracion and the target's nervous field.

insectoid.name: Archnida
insectoid.note: Genetic splice of spider, insect, bear, and human DNA — created as weapons of war; partially reclaimed after Tauron-87. Bipedal through Polypedal · Large–Colossal (7–16 ft, average 10). Neck-to-ground mandibles; hollow arm chambers with retractable diamond-hard inner limbs.

abilities.name: Bursting Fracture
abilities.effect: Target: 1 Creature · Vector: Strike · Instant · Resolution: Endurance Check · Limit: once per turn. On a successful attack, the target must make an Endurance Check. Failure = an immediate follow-up attack is triggered automatically. The follow-up cannot itself trigger Bursting Fracture.

abilities.name: Unnerving Presence
abilities.effect: Target: Multi · Vector: Ambient · Duration: 1 round · Area: determined proximity · Resolution: d20 + Size Modifier (+2 per 2 ft of height above 7 ft) · Limit: once per scene, on reveal or first melee closure. All creatures within the determined proximity roll against your presence; the result's margin sets which Disadvantage is imposed — light (next check), moderate (all checks vs you this round), or severe (Feared 1 round).

insectoid.name: Cerioisk
insectoid.note: Born during the Witching Moon from a dying Seed's essence fused with a decaying Kinba body — 'the death that learns'. Bipedal, evolving multi-limbed through Cocoon Phases · Moderate–Large (1.8–3.5 m). Do not age or die naturally; only sealing halts them. Existential-tier threat classification.

abilities.name: Augo Consumption
abilities.effect: Target: 1 creature possessing an Augo Gland · Vector: Contact · Instant · Automatic. Absorb the Augo Gland of any creature that possesses one. Every 10th Gland absorbed triggers a Cocoon Phase: the Cerioisk enters dormancy and emerges with adaptive traits and an increase to all core stats. Cap: +1 per stat per Cocoon Phase, and Phases resolve during Downtime — the death that learns still has to sleep.

abilities.name: Corruptive Reproduction
abilities.effect: Target: 1 consumed gland-bearer · Vector: Contact · Duration: Clock (one Downtime) · Automatic. When a creature with an Augo Gland is consumed by a Cerioisk, a new Cerioisk is produced from the digested remains. It is Curator-run — kin rather than servant — and matures over one Downtime.

insectoid.name: Venarian
insectoid.note: Venarians are humanoid-presenting Insectoids that generally stand within the Moderate–Large range. Their faces possess four mandibles — two upper and two lower — with the lower pair forming what appears to be an ordinary Human-like jaw when closed. When separated, the mandibles expose multiple rows of teeth beneath an otherwise convincing set of lips, jaw, and chin. Chitinous plating covers portions of the shoulders, forearms, chest, abdomen, thighs, calves, shins, ankles, neck, jaw, and temples. These plates frequently terminate in jagged or serrated edges that function as natural blades. Bipedal · Moderate–Large. Serrated Natural Weapons: successful physical attacks made with Venarian mandibles or chitin blades apply Serration. While Serration applies, subsequent physical damage against that target ignores 50% of its Defensive HP (DHP) when determining how much damage reaches the protected Health Pool. Natural Chitin: attacks striking the Venarian's chitinous armor cannot bypass, ignore, or negate its DHP through ordinary armor-penetration effects. Damage that successfully reaches the chitin is reduced by 1d6 + Endurance Modifier. Effects that explicitly bypass species anatomy or deal damage that ignores DHP entirely still function normally. Venarian culture places considerable importance on the physical remnants of defeated foes. A trophy is not valued simply because something died; its meaning comes from the hunt, the circumstances of the kill, and the relationship between hunter and prey. Their outwardly humanoid appearance often conceals a much more predatory anatomy until the mandibles separate or the chitinous edges of the body are brought to bear.

abilities.name: Primed Instinct
abilities.effect: Type: Passive (Self, Reaction) · Area: 20 ft · Duration: Instant · Resolution: Mental Save — Perception using Wisdom instead of Intelligence. The Venarian possesses a natural danger sense capable of recognizing hostile, damaging, or otherwise harmful phenomena that enter within 20 ft. This sense reveals the presence and immediate direction of danger, but does not automatically identify the source, exact ability, or intentions behind it. When the Venarian becomes subject to an incoming harmful effect detected by Primed Instinct, they may make a Mental Save — Perception using Wisdom instead of Intelligence against the incoming resolution. If the effect has no opposing roll, use its listed DV or a Curator-set DV. On success, the Venarian gains Advantage on the first defensive Check or Save they make against that same effect. If the effect normally allows no defensive resolution, Primed Instinct does not create one.

abilities.name: Trophy Collector
abilities.effect: Target: 1 Corpse · Vector: Contact / Crafting · Duration: Permanent · Resolution: Automatic; weapon actions use their natural Roll Paths. Venarians are traditional headhunters who preserve the remnants of worthy foes as functional trophies. Given access to the corpse of a creature they helped defeat, a Venarian may curate its remains into a Trophy Weapon whose form is determined by the usable anatomy and materials of the corpse. A Trophy Weapon may inherit one primary Trophy Trait derived from the creature it was made from — such as a biological weapon, defensive property, sensory adaptation, elemental expression, or another characteristic the Curator determines can reasonably survive translation into a weapon. The inherited trait does not consume Neuronal Capacity simply for being wielded. Trophy Weapons still make attacks, impose effects, and resist interference through their own natural Checks, Saves, Roll Paths, damage, and limits. The corpse is consumed by the crafting process. A Trophy Weapon normally possesses only one inherited Trophy Trait unless an explicit effect or Curator ruling allows otherwise. (The Curator determines the potency and fidelity of the Trophy Trait from the Venarian's actual contribution to defeating the creature, the method by which the creature was felled, the strength of the defeated creature, and the difference in capability between hunter and prey. A Venarian who personally overcame a stronger opponent produces a substantially more faithful trophy than one taken from a creature they barely participated in defeating.)

subdermin.name: Fractine
subdermin.note: Crystalline beings born from Alteria's mineral-rich geodes fused with SubDermin bio-energies. Bipedal (crystalline quadrupedal brace under duress) · Moderate–Large. Diamond-like, self-repairing crystalline structure. Culture values endurance above all.

abilities.name: Diamond Form
abilities.effect: Self (Reaction) · Duration: 1 round · Automatic · Limit: once per scene. Enter a near-impervious crystalline physical state: resistant to kinetic and elemental damage types, reflecting a portion (1d6) of received damage back at the attacker. While in the state your movement is 0.

abilities.name: Crystal Manipulation
abilities.effect: Target: Objects / Area · Vector: Contact · Duration: Sustained (combat projections) or permanent (built structures) · Automatic. Form barriers, weapons, or structures from surrounding crystal matter; combat projections are temporary, while structures given sufficient uninterrupted time become permanent. Crystal constructs follow object rules — demolition applies.

subdermin.name: Construct
subdermin.note: SubDermin's most catastrophic experiment — condensed life energy housed in composite alloy and Barion matter. Bipedal · Always Large. Endures sun-surface temperatures; survives catastrophic damage; may inherit emotional bleed from consumed source souls. Interitus Enmortem weapons are the sole known counter.

abilities.name: Physical Fracture
abilities.effect: Target: 1 Creature · Vector: Strike · Instant · Damage: equal to the first hit's damage · Resolution: Endurance Check ends the Anchor · Limit: once per round. On a successful physical attack, a second amplified strike triggers automatically, dealing damage equal to the first hit. If the second strike's total exceeds the target's combined defensive and offensive power, the target becomes Anchored — forced prone, unable to reposition until passing an Endurance Check.

abilities.name: Pressuring Advance
abilities.effect: Target: Multi · Vector: Wave · Instant · Area: Radius 50 ft of the destination point · Resolution: Balance Check and Endurance Save · Limit: once per scene. Bonus Action: move at half speed in a burst. All creatures within 50 feet of the destination point must make both checks or suffer stagger (Staggered, pushed 10 ft).

subdermin.name: Trevant
subdermin.note: Trevant developed from SubDermin communities that became increasingly shamanic and mystic in their relationship with the natural world. Rather than allowing their radiation to remain purely corrosive or ambient, they learned to infuse surrounding earth and flora with it. Over time, this altered radiation became capable of stimulating growth, awakening plant life, and eventually granting sentience to flora. The greatest expressions of this practice were the first Trevants — towering living trees that became protectors, gathering places, and even homes for other creatures. Bipedal; may passively shift between Full Trevant Form and Hybrid Form · Tiny–Colossal. Radiant Growth: flora within 100 ft of the Trevant is continuously stimulated by their altered SubDermin radiation and grows at an accelerated rate. This growth does not automatically damage, restrain, heal, or otherwise resolve against creatures unless another ability specifically uses it. Full Trevant Form: the body takes on the form of a living tree with functional arms and legs. Hybrid Form: the body becomes substantially more humanoid while retaining botanical anatomy; some Trevant can appear close to Human, including the development of conventional-looking skin. Trevant are often regarded as mighty but unusually gentle beings. Their cultures place heavy emphasis on honor, hospitality, respect, and the protection of living communities. Larger Trevant frequently become literal homes or sanctuaries for creatures with nowhere else to go, and many Trevant settlements treat the act of sheltering another living being as a sacred responsibility.

abilities.name: Vhisper
abilities.effect: Target: 1 Flora · Vector: Contact · Duration: 1 Indefinite / 2 last for 2 turns · Resolution: Automatic · Limit: maximum 3 active Vespants. As a Standard Action, touch a living piece of flora and awaken it into a sentient botanical creature called a Vespant. A Vespant may move and perform simple actions independently, and the Trevant may perceive through its senses remotely with no set range. Any Check or Save performed by a Vespant resolves through the natural Roll Path of the action it attempts. When one of your Vespants is destroyed by a hostile creature or an environmental effect, roll 1d40 and store the result as Returned Vitality. The Trevant can restore a Health Pool that is not full, add the stored value to that restoration, then consume it.

abilities.name: Vitam
abilities.effect: Type: Passive Trigger · Target: Self / Nearby Flora · Area: within 10 ft of your Vespants · Duration: Until expended · Resolution: Automatic · Limit: once per Vespant. Once per Vespant, when flora within your Radiant Growth area meaningfully expands, blooms, or is newly created, roll 1d10 and create a Vitam Pool equal to the result. If a Vitam Pool already exists, the new roll adds onto the currently existing Pool. The next time you restore one of your Health Pools, you may consume the Vitam Pool and add its value to that restoration. If one of your Vespants was destroyed by a hostile creature or environmental effect within your previous 3 Actions, you may instead consume the Vitam Pool when you successfully deal damage. Add the stored value as Raw Damage to that attack or damaging ability. The original attack still resolves through its normal Check, Save, Roll Path, damage, and limits.

subdermin.name: Salaris
subdermin.note: Through prolonged experimentation, SubDermin subjects were forced through successive stages of accelerated evolution using the gene expression of Human DNA. The procedure succeeded only on the surface. Their outward bodies became Human in appearance, but internally the SubDermin genome prevailed, reconstructing Human anatomy through mineral equivalents. Salaris are therefore externally Human-looking beings whose organs and bodily fluids are composed almost entirely of mineral structures. Bipedal; externally Human in appearance · Moderate. Salaris possess ordinary-looking Human skin, eyes, nails, hands, feet, hair, and other external features. Internally, however, their anatomy is mineral rather than conventionally organic: organs, circulatory material, and several internal fluids have been reconstructed as specialized mineral equivalents. Disconnected from typical SubDermin radiation control — all radiation-based abilities grant Advantage on Mental Check — Capacity (Intelligence), and radiation is expressed as elemental energy. Mineral Configuration: Crystalline Brain (dense Diamond-Crystal composite; first time each Scene falling below 65 SS, immediately recover flat 40 SS), Iron Heart (raw Iron; intense heat), Bismuth Lungs (layered Bismuth; Shimmering Breath), Saline Blood (white murky mineral suspension; crystallizes into salt on oxygen exposure), Radiant Spinal Fluid (liquefied SubDermin radiation). Salaris possess extraordinary potential and are regarded by many Human and SubDermin institutions as abominations born from failed attempts at forced refinement. Despite this reputation, numerous Salaris have become the subjects of legends — including stories of individuals whose Shimmering Breath and mineral expression produced winters that covered entire worlds. Salaris communities tend to be tightly knit and fiercely protective of one another. Their frightening internal biology stands in sharp contrast to a cultural reputation for unusual compassion and deeply communal bonds.

abilities.name: Iudicius
abilities.effect: Target: Multi · Vector: Crystal Formation · Duration: Instant / Sustained Anchor · Resolution: Mental Check — Capacity vs Physical Save — Evasion; Physical Check — Power escapes the pillar · Limit: requires at least one crystallized Salaris formation within Reach. As a Bonus Action, launch one or more crystallized salt formations within Reach. Make a Mental Check — Capacity (Intelligence); creatures in their path make a Physical Save — Evasion. On a failed Save, targets become Hard Anchored, and each connecting formation absorbs 5 SS (additional formations +5 SS) stored in the pillar per pillar. Hard Anchored creatures can break free with a Physical Check — Power, or the Salaris may reabsorb pillars to reclaim stored SS. Destroyed pillars lose any stored SS (while they have SS inside of them, they cannot be imbued with anything external or internal besides their base effects).

abilities.name: Rudam
abilities.effect: Target: Self / Created Mineral Structures · Vector: Emission · Duration: Instant creation; structures persist normally · Resolution: Mental Check — Capacity · Limit: applies only to crystalline or mineral structures produced from the Salaris body. As a Bonus Action, the Salaris may enlarge, multiply, or project any crystalline structure from their body and or produce, requiring a Mental Check — Capacity. At DV 10, one Moderate formation within 10 ft can be created or enlarged; each 5 points above DV 10 grants an additional Growth option: extra formation, increase Size Class, or extend projection by 100 ft roll (1d10) for feet. Multiple Growths can be combined. Rudam does not deal damage directly; effects resolve via natural Roll Path.

inderi.name: AI'N
inderi.note: Beings of pure mental and spiritual data, born from the Implosion of the First Universe and given form under Protocol Evangeline. No fixed form — inhabit machinery, data streams, and minds; manifested form is Small. Forcibly integrated into vessels (T-BM001) by Indrah; documentation expunged; believed extinct.

abilities.name: Dilation
abilities.effect: Self (Reaction) · Instant · Automatic · Limit: once per round. On failing an AP Check, slow perceived time for incoming attacks; gain Advantage on the next roll made in response.

abilities.name: Replication
abilities.effect: Target: 1 remembered object, construct, or being · Vector: Gaze · Duration: Clock (once per 2 in-universe hours) · Resolution: the target of replication contests with a Control + Inspiration Skill Check against the AI'N's DC; the process cannot fail on the AI'N's side. Manifest a flawless 1:1 replica of any remembered object, construct, or being — only the target's contest can degrade the copy. Caps: a replicated being is an inert, mindless shell — data has no soul to copy; Ciphers, charges, and DNA-locks never replicate.

inderi.name: Aeor
inderi.note: Little is known about the Aeor beyond that they began appearing from different parts of the Multiverse and slowly integrated. They are small and resemble the imps of mystical tales, yet genetic testing shows they descend from all sorts of different species. They are theorised to come from the Great Conscientia — that an Inderi's deep desire for freedom led to their creation. Because of how the Inderi work, the Aeor tend to permeate as energy unless locked down, so the catalyst keeping them here has permeated throughout the Weave, solidifying them. Bipedal; Tiny to Small. They can enlarge parts of their body — not physically, but energetically, surging their atoms with tense energy in a controlled manner so they can project energy constructs from designated parts of the body, though never the entire body, for long periods.

abilities.name: Tru
abilities.effect: Type: Self (Standard) · Duration: Instant · Resolution: Automatic · Limit: once per turn. During any action, spend a Bonus Action to inflict another extension of that action, described through their projected form. The projected form has double the movement of the standard creature but half the reach.

abilities.name: Induction
abilities.effect: Target: 1 remembered object, construct, or being · Vector: Gaze · Duration: until cancelled · Resolution: Automatic. The Aeor destabilises structures — the energy around them, not the physical structure itself. Any energy entering their Zone of Influence — 40 feet for an Aeor, rather than the standard 30 — can be contested, forcing a Control Check that must beat the Aeor's DC. On a failure the energy is rendered unstable and they are blasted back, up to half the reach of the Aeor's projected energy form.

inderi.name: Inderelict
inderi.note: Embodied remnants believed to answer the Inderi's ancient worship of the e’Inderitch. During a period of abandonment and persecution, the Inderi collective called The Ender prayed for deliverance; soon after, meteorites known as Eyis began falling across the Eastern and Northern Sectors carrying the first Inderelict. Whether they are true remnants, manifestations produced by belief, or something else entirely remains unknown. Bipedal · Moderate–Large. Eyis Pearl: pearl-like Eyis deposits embed throughout the body, disintegrating the original Augo Gland and assuming its function. Inderelict cannot suffer ordinary Hollow Body Syndrome, but may suffer Malignant Hollow Body Syndrome. Inderelict embody a ritual logic of revelation and recognition: Venyl grants perception and protection, Vepred offers release, and Gualus punishes the failure to relinquish the gift. Their connection to the original e’Inderitch remains unverified.

abilities.name: Venyl
abilities.effect: Type: Standard Action / Reaction · Target: 1 other creature · Range: Reach · Duration: until released · Resolution: Mental Check — Capacity vs Mental Save — Influence · Limit: one Venyl target at a time; cannot target self. On a failed Save, the target gains Energy Vision, may perceive normally with its eyes closed, restores 15 SS at the start of each turn during an active Scene, and cannot gain new mental effects from sources other than the originating Inderelict. Existing mental effects remain. The Inderelict may speak Vepred during its Action window. The target then has until the end of its next turn to repeat Vepred. Doing so ends Venyl safely. Failure to answer ends Venyl's benefits and gives the target Hollow Body Syndrome, making it eligible for Gualus.

abilities.name: Gualus
abilities.effect: Type: Bonus Action · Target: 1 creature that failed your Vepred sequence · Range: Reach · Duration: Special · Resolution: Automatic · Limit: once per failed Venyl sequence. Speak Gualus to a target carrying Hollow Body Syndrome from your Venyl. An Eyis pearl encapsulates its Augo Gland, replacing the condition with Malignant Hollow Body Syndrome; the target also loses ordinary sight and the ability to speak. In combat, this sensory suppression ends at the beginning of the target's next turn or immediately if another creature audibly speaks a Recognized Name the target genuinely accepts as referring to itself. Outside combat, it persists until such a name is spoken. A Recognized Name may be a personal name, title, callsign, designation, or other stable identifier — it is not a metaphysical true name. The originating Inderelict cannot satisfy this requirement. Restoring sight and speech does not remove Malignant Hollow Body Syndrome or the Eyis pearl.

inderi.name: Mem'oretha
inderi.note: Seclusive Inderi whose identities and original forms have deteriorated through prolonged Eldritch exposure. Their bodies persist as unstable impressions of Hyomen anatomy — swathing, inconsistent energy continuously attempting to remember what a body should be. Most stabilize themselves inside crafted shells of composite, rare, or ornate materials. These shells commonly imitate Hyomen physiology, but may omit, duplicate, enlarge, or replace features according to the Mem'oretha's preferred identity. As they age, information enters their minds without any clear source, granting knowledge unrelated to their lived experience; whether these memories belong to themselves, other beings, or Eldritch space remains unknown. Bipedal · Moderate. Whenever an Augo Gland within 10 ft expends Synaptic Space to activate or maintain an Eldritch ability, regain HP equal to half of the SS spent. If HP is full, restore DHP instead; if both are full, nothing is gained. Only creature-generated Eldritch energy produced through an Augo Gland qualifies — ambient Eldritch phenomena, environmental anomalies, and non-Augo sources do not. Mem'oretha exist between recollection and embodiment. Creature-generated Eldritch energy repairs the body, while ambient Eldritch energy reinforces identity. Breaking the shell does not weaken them so much as remove the structure forcing them to remain recognizably person-shaped.

abilities.name: Hearth of the Old
abilities.effect: Type: Self (Active / Sustained) · Duration: Sustained · Resolution: Automatic · Limit: 7 active rounds per Long Rest. Draw ambient Eldritch information into the unstable consciousness, provided the energy does not originate from another creature. At the end of each round sustained, gain 1 Memory Token. Each Memory Token grants +1 Base Intelligence — this modifies the Attribute itself, not its modifier, and therefore naturally alters any statistics legitimately derived from Intelligence. Normally hold a maximum of 5 Memory Tokens. Tokens remain until the end of the Scene unless another effect states otherwise.

abilities.name: Horseman
abilities.effect: Type: Passive · Trigger: DHP reaches 0 · Target: Self · Duration: Scene · Resolution: Automatic · Limit: once per Scene. When DHP reaches 0, the crafted body fractures and the Eldritch form beneath it is exposed. Immediately gain 2 Memory Tokens and increase the maximum held from 5 to 7 for the remainder of the Scene. While Horseman is active, physical Reach becomes 40 ft + 5 ft per Memory Token, incoming Eldritch damage is reduced by 25%, and Movement gains a flat +15. The exposed body may reshape into any physically coherent configuration that can reasonably be created within its current Reach; this reshaping does not inherently change Attributes, Derived Statistics, number of Actions, or grant new biological abilities. Restoring DHP does not end Horseman once triggered.

seraph.name: Fallen Seraph
seraph.note: Seraph stripped of their Antimatter Wings through exile, sacrifice, or catastrophic conflict — relentless terrestrial combatants. Bipedal (glowing wing-scar tissue) · Moderate (6'2"–7'0"). Divine Scar (recessive): antimatter burns that faintly illuminate under stress. Spatial Acuity (dominant): Seraph spatial awareness remains intact.

abilities.name: Scar Beam
abilities.effect: Target: 1 Creature · Vector: Wave (Line 60 ft) · Instant · Damage: Antimatter equal to (Int + Neuronal Capacity Modifier) · Resolution: Dexterity save, half · Limit: three times per encounter. Fire concentrated antimatter from the severed wing-stumps in a precise 60-ft beam. Requires no additional action when incorporated into a Standard Action attack.

abilities.name: Grounded Insight
abilities.effect: Passive (Self) · Always · Area: 60 ft · Automatic. Permanent Advantage on tactical and terrain rolls within 60 feet. Ground-level environments are always treated as familiar terrain.

seraph.name: Ardent Seraph
seraph.note: Seraph whose continual manipulation of space fractured their own existence — flickering across overlapping coordinates while drawing reality toward them. Bipedal (intermittently multi-positional) · Moderate–Large (apparent size fluctuates). Spatial Bleed (recessive): may awaken elsewhere from unconsciousness. Dimensional Sensitivity (dominant): exceptional awareness of dimensional seams.

abilities.name: Fracture Point
abilities.effect: Self · Duration: until the encounter ends · Automatic · Limit: maximum three active anchors; one teleport per round. Place invisible spatial anchors within 60 feet as a Free Action. Teleport to any active anchor as a Bonus Action.

abilities.name: Reality Pull
abilities.effect: Target: Creatures or Objects within 30 ft · Vector: Gaze · Instant · Resolution: unwilling targets make a Strength Save against the Ardent Seraph's Control DC. Pull creatures or objects within 30 feet directly adjacent. Objects up to Large size move automatically.

seraph.name: Oris
seraph.note: The culmination of the once-Orialia and the new Seraph. Bipedal · Tiny or Colossal. Always surrounded by Stardust — used for mobility, moving with it and flying at half Movement Speed.

abilities.name: Localized Pocket
abilities.effect: At Will — Out of Combat / Reaction / Bonus Action · Vector: Anchor · Duration: Sustained · Automatic · Limit: one Phenomenon stored at a time; stored Phenomena fade at scene's end; you cannot Store an effect whose Synaptic cost exceeds your Control stat. While not in active combat, generate a Localized Pocket Space that any part of your body may enter. Upon entering, choose one: Connect — link the Pocket Space to a second space within 65 feet of you. Store — absorb the effect of a Phenomenon that was targeted at you, holding it within the Pocket Space for later use. Redirect — release a stored Phenomenon outward through any other Localized Pocket Space within 50 feet of you. Store and Redirect may each be triggered as a Reaction or a Bonus Action.

abilities.name: Stardust Resurgence
abilities.effect: Target: 1 Creature · Vector: Strike · Instant · Damage: automatic follow-up attack at +5 damage · Resolution: Automatic when thresholds are met · Limit: once per round. When you make an attack, you may generate Stardust to trigger an automatic follow-up attack dealing +5 damage — only if your Attack Power and Neuronal Capacity are both higher than the target's corresponding values. If your Action Priority and Evasion each exceed the target's by more than 10 points, this may instead be triggered as a Reaction in place of your normal attack action.

seraph.name: Riftwalkers
seraph.note: Seraphs who closely resemble their branch's origins — descendants of a greater plane who venture into the mirror realm and bring forth its unstable energy. Bipedal · Moderate (~5 ft). They passively teleport with every step (no mechanical effect). A rare sight in the light of day.

abilities.name: Portalweave
abilities.effect: Self (Active) · Duration: Special · Automatic · Limit: once per round. Open a controlled, lingering portal and enter a rift into a sub-realm of our own; within it, energy fluctuates so frequently that perception is heightened — as if time stopped in the outside world. You may move up to your max movement; any action or exhausting that movement ends this ability and leaves another portal behind at your exit. While inside, the outside world is truly un-interactable — no attacking out, no scouting through barriers you could not otherwise pass.

abilities.name: Anti-Matter Discharge
abilities.effect: Target: Single / Line · Vector: Wave (Line 50 ft) · Instant · Damage: 2d10 Antimatter · Resolution: Dexterity save, half · Limit: twice per encounter. Any connecting portals can emit energy from the dimension they are from: shoot a beam up to 50 feet from an open portal, or channel it between two connected portals. Can be used after exiting a portal, or while placing one down with Portalweave.

stygians.name: Xeno
stygians.note: Engineered Stygian offshoot for biological warfare — the 'Ghosts of Flesh'. Bipedal (tall, emaciated, serpentine) · Colossal (Lanky). Retractable inner proboscis/tongue extends up to 60 ft; excretes viscous black fluid on contact. Covertly allied with the N-T1 through the Deviants faction.

abilities.name: Mutagenic Absorption
abilities.effect: Target: 1 living creature · Vector: Contact · Duration: Instant · Resolution: Endurance save; extent by Curator ruling · Limit: once per scene per target. Excretes black viscous fluid on contact with living tissue, causing genetic destabilization and unpredictable mutations in the target. Caps: mutations are minor-to-hindering, never lethal, and never permanent without the target's player consenting.

abilities.name: Freakish Nature
abilities.effect: Self (Reaction) · Duration: Scene · Resolution: Adaptation Skill Check vs Curator-set DC. If the tongue/proboscis is severed, make the check: if the result exceeds the DC, the tongue regenerates — into multiple tongues equal to half the check result (cap: maximum 3), each able to hold or strike independently until the scene ends.

stygians.name: Greys
stygians.note: Stygians tempered by the Doalith Dominion into peaceful, psychically enhanced beings. Bipedal humanoid · Moderate (~5 ft). Pale grey skin; large reflective psionic eyes; intelligence far above baseline. Currently in mass psionic dormancy after contact with the Indrah consciousness.

abilities.name: Telepathy
abilities.effect: Target: Single or network · Vector: Gaze · Duration: Sustained · Resolution: Wisdom save (unwilling). Communicate telepathically as a bonus or prepared action (or freely outside combat). Also functions as telekinesis: move objects weighing up to (2 × Neuronal Capacity Modifier + Control stat) — never as a direct attack.

abilities.name: Psionic Mold
abilities.effect: Target: Self or 1 organic form · Vector: Contact · Duration: Scene · Resolution: Automatic (self); Endurance save (others) · Limit: +1 Fatigue per use beyond the first each scene. Psionically reshape organic matter — including your own body: adjust muscle density, alter facial features, seal wounds (ends one Bleeding effect). Versatile for infiltration and healing; extended use is draining.

stygians.name: Annunaki
stygians.note: Near-mythological species of uncertain lineage who walk between realities; only faint Stygian genetic echoes. Bipedal · Moderate–Large (6–10 ft standard; rare outliers 12–15 ft). Head shape chosen at creation grants one additional ability. Melamic energy is not one of the 5 standard Genera.

ability.name: Telepathy
ability.effect: Identical mechanics to the Greys' Telepathy ability — telepathic comms and telekinesis (up to 2 × Neuronal Capacity Modifier + Control stat), never as a direct attack.

ability.name: Precognition
ability.effect: Precognitive vision — Advantage on all AP Rolls made against opponents of lower Neuronal Capacity Modifier.

ability.name: Atomic Manipulation
ability.effect: Reshape matter by touch; usable once per hour (cap: unattended objects, Small or smaller — never creatures or held gear).

abilities.name: Melam Manifestation
abilities.effect: Self (Reaction) · Duration: Instant · Resolution: attacker's Control Skill Check vs the Annunaki's DC · Limit: 1 free use per round; additional uses cost Synaptic Space. Emit a Melamic Energy Field defensive shield when attacked. If the attacker fails the check, the attack warps to a random location within 10 feet of you or them (Curator rolls).

abilities.name: Ni Conjuration
abilities.effect: Target: Area · Vector: Ambient · Duration: Sustained · Damage: the conjured element's standard type dice · Resolution: per conjured effect; scale per Curator discretion · Limit: one element at a time. Psionic command over a single element present in the current environment — shape, hurl, or wall it. Ni commands what exists; it does not create.

stygians.name: Sbeindlaer
stygians.note: Descendants of the one who cast the 'Blight Night'. Bipedal humanoid · Moderate (~5 ft). Two skin layers: a controllable outer black void layer (projectile/chitin, regenerates; usage 25% of max HP; range per tile × 2) and a highly blightful inner dark-grey layer. Unique: DHP is a flat additive on the outer layer, integrated into the main health bar.

abilities.name: Unstable Blightness
abilities.effect: Target: Multi · Vector: Ambient (your shadow) · Duration: Sustained · Damage: decay = (Control + Priority) ÷ 15 per turn, absorbed to regenerate your outer layer · Resolution: Endurance save halves that turn's decay. Those who step into your shadows are rapidly decayed and absorbed to regenerate a portion of your outer layer. Inflicts one blight stack per round of exposure, increasing additively by 1 per consecutive round. Upon reaching 8 stacks the blight ruptures: 3d10 Entropy and Incapacitated 1 round, then stacks reset to 4 (Incapacitated 1 hour of passive time outside combat).

abilities.name: Dream Eater
abilities.effect: Target: 1 sleeping creature · Vector: Ambient (outer layer or mind) · Duration: Sustained · Damage: 1d8 Psychic or 1d10 Spirit per round · Resolution: Wisdom save each round ends the invasion. Invade the consciousness of those asleep: harm their soul/mind at the listed rate, prolong their slumber, or communicate within the dream. Caps: the target visibly dreams in distress — observers can wake them, ending the invasion; a target reduced below half HP by Dream Eater wakes automatically. It wounds; it never kills the sleeping.
